summary: WHY is the tree ~2.4x slower than native at B=4 SWE? MEASURED per-forward decomposition (NOT TPS/accept hand-rolling) - weight-stream vs attention vs GDN-scan vs tree-machinery; removable kernel tax vs fundamental. CPU on measured artifacts.

synthesis.gap_root_measured:
MEASURED-ONLY HEADLINE (basis = decode_seconds, a raw vLLM counter; NOT wall, because tree emitted only 1856 vs 2048 tokens so wall_s=2.074x understates tree). decode_seconds ratio tree/native = 298.497/127.755 = 2.336x. This factors EXACTLY into two independently-measured counters (neither is TPS/accept):

  2.336x = (a) MORE FORWARDS x (b) MORE TIME PER FORWARD
         = (spec_drafts 620/433 = 1.432x) x (decode_seconds/spec_drafts: 0.4814 / 0.2950 s = 1.632x)
  Check: 1.432 x 1.632 = 2.336. Verified against artifacts.

Log-share of the decode gap: ~42% from MORE FORWARDS (accept gap), ~58% from MORE TIME PER FORWARD (per-forward tax). So the gap is NOT primarily an acceptance problem; it is roughly even, with the slightly larger share being the slower verifier forward.

What is MEASURED vs UNKNOWN:
- MEASURED (raw counters, scripts/fr12_deliverable_swe4_probe.py before/after /metrics scrape): both factors. (a) spec_drafts = forward count (confirmed: spec_draft_tokens/spec_drafts = exactly 9.000 in both arms = num_spec_tokens, so one draft event == one verifier forward). (b) per-forward time = decode_seconds/spec_drafts, both fields measured -- this is the legitimate, allowed per-forward quantity, NOT TPS/accept (the banned 1.412x/1.29x form is avoided).
- The accept gap is itself measured and corroborated: accepted/event = 3.794 (native) vs 2.024 (tree); reject_step_counts modal at step-0 (tree mostly accepts spine-only).
- UNKNOWN/un-isolatable from these 7 counters: decode_seconds is a per-request SUM under B=4 concurrency (windows overlap), so the 1.632x per-forward is a correct RELATIVE ratio but its absolute s/draft is not single-stream forward latency, and it cannot be split into kernel-time vs B=4 co-scheduling vs preemption. No request_metrics.jsonl and no steptrace exist in the run dir, so per-layer/per-kernel attribution of the 1.632x is NOT measured.
synthesis.removable_vs_fundamental:
Per-forward tax split (the 1.632x), removable-by-tuning vs fundamental. Forward is weight-bandwidth-bound: 27 GB fp8 / 273 GB/s = 98.9 ms floor on GB10, so a change only moves wall-time if it cuts HBM bytes or removes wasted launches.

REMOVABLE (kernel tuning / rewrite) -- the dominant tree-specific adder:
- GDN tree-scan per-node STATE traffic = the LARGEST adder. Kernel materializes a per-node fp32 state for all 9 tree nodes vs native's single carried state = 9x state r+w amplification: +8.95% of the 27 GB weight stream per request, +35.8% at B=4 (LABELED ESTIMATE: CPU cost-model /tmp/gdn_cost_verify.py, not GPU-measured). Two sub-parts:
   * The h_cache register spill (128 KB/program > GB10 255-reg cap at 4 warps) is REMOVABLE-BY-TUNING and ALREADY FIXED: num_warps=8 committed at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:582 (a586ac84) -> 128 regs/lane, hard overrun gone. (CAVEAT: ptxas spill-bytes==0 re-confirm + bit-exact re-check at N_PAD=16 are still LIVE gates, not GPU-certified.)
   * The remaining 9x state r+w is NOT a flag -- removable ONLY by a kernel rewrite (WY one-pass / recompute-from-spine, accept-only state commit), proven lossless on CPU (fp32 4.19e-9, 0 argmax flips). This is the #1 do-now lever. So this adder is removable-by-rewrite, structural-not-fundamental.
- TREE_ATTN vs FA2: the stock Triton TREE_ATTN is less-tuned (base-e exp vs FA2 exp2+folded-scale), but this is a NUMERIC/lossless cost (~0.00195/layer), NOT per-forward time -- attention is ~0.1% of a bandwidth-bound forward and is hidden behind the weight stream. Removed by the FA2 -inf-bias fork (a tuned TREE_ATTN), ~time-neutral by design.
- Eager-launch tax: bounded ~2.7% of the 98.9 ms floor (384 launches x ~7us); full CUDA-graph capture removes it. (LABELED ESTIMATE; whether the verify forward is fully captured on cu130-nightly is unresolved -- if eager, this is a real but small tree-specific adder.)

FUNDAMENTAL (cannot remove without losing the tree / losslessness):
- Attention node-count: tree verifies 36 positions/forward at B=4 vs native's 24 (9-node tree vs 5-chain) -- more attention work scales with node count. But it is hidden behind the bandwidth floor and does not move GB10 wall-time.
- No-copy FA2 -inf-bias: in-register elementwise add into the MMA accumulator -- NO extra pass/kernel/MMA (~324 B L1-resident bias). Negligible time; leaves only a ~1-bf16-ULP grouping floor (0.0039 on 2 of ~983k elements) that is FUNDAMENTAL to no-copy scattered KV but far under the E5 self-noise floor (~0.059), so lossless and free.
- Committer gather/scatter: once per decode step (not per layer), <=5 accepted rows; ~0.47% of weight stream (LABELED ESTIMATE, my arithmetic). Negligible.
synthesis.can_tree_be_faster:
Marginal-to-unlikely on the current 9-node caterpillar; possible only if BOTH a kernel win AND a real branch-accept win land together. Governing identity: TPS = (accept/event + 1) / time_per_forward. Break-even needs accept_tree >= (accept_native+1)*(t_tree/t_nat) - 1, with native accept/event = 3.794.

Break-even accept/event the tree must hit (LABELED: structural-forward estimates):
- at 1.00x forward (all tax removed): >= 3.794 (must match native AND branches must be free).
- at 1.10x forward (clean, GDN-state amp removed): >= 4.27 (+13%).
- at 1.13x forward (KERNEL doc clean structural est): >= 4.42 (+16.5%).
- at the MEASURED contaminated 1.632x forward: >= 6.82 -- IMPOSSIBLE on a depth-5 spine (ceiling 5.0).

Two hard facts cap the upside:
1. Native MTP-5 is a depth-5 chain with HARD accept/event ceiling 5.0; native 3.794 = 75.9% saturated -- the literature (Multi-Draft 2410.18234, OPT-Tree 2406.17276) says native nearly saturates the ceiling, so a lossless tree's upside is a THIN slice. Losslessness/bit-exactness contributes ZERO to speed (it's a constraint).
2. In EVERY measured run, branches added 0 net accepts (pos5-8 survival = 0). So the realized branch upside has been zero vs the +0.48-to-0.62 needed -- and the caterpillar drafter has two known bugs (propose_tree builds 2 parallel chains not a caterpillar; deep-spine GDN-flat), so the branches may simply be starved/garbage.

The single lever that touches the binding metric is removing the kernel tax (WY one-pass) to pull tree forward from 1.632x(contaminated)/~1.13x(clean est) toward ~1.0-1.05x. But even at 1.0x, the tree only wins if branches start adding real accepts -- which is unproven. So tree-faster is conditional and currently capped, not demonstrated. WY is PARKED (failed literal-0.0, never re-measured at the within-floor bar). The clean re-measurement (FR10_METRICS off, FR12/13 hooks compiled out, WY kernel) is the unrun arbiter.
synthesis.speed_levers_ranked:
1. REMOVE THE KERNEL TAX (WY one-pass + accept-only state commit) -- THE ONLY lever with measured headroom on the binding metric. Removes the GDN-state 9x->1x amplification (+8.95% to +35.8% of the weight stream at B=4) LOSSLESSLY (fp32 4.19e-9, 0 argmax flips). Drives tree time/forward from 1.632x toward ~1.0-1.05x. Recovers AT MOST the per-forward 58% share of the gap; the num_warps=8 spill fix is already in. This is the #1 do-now item (WY currently PARKED, sequential rank-1 scan is live).

2. DEEPER DRAFTER (depth 6/7/8) -- RAISES the accept/event ceiling (depth-d chain ceiling = d.0), the only way past the 5.0 cap. Real headroom but it is a DRAFTER change, ORTHOGONAL to the verify kernel, with its own per-token accept decay and an added forward cost per depth. Out-of-scope for the FR10/13 tree-verify deliverable but the genuine route to acc/event > native.

3. CLOSE THE ACCEPT GAP / FIX THE DRAFTER (recover the 1.432x more-forwards factor) -- caps at ~42% of the decode gap and only IF branches start contributing. On a 76%-saturated depth-5 spine the marginal accept a fixed caterpillar buys is small; gated entirely on fixing the two drafter topology bugs. Lower headroom than (1).

4. MORE BRANCHES / WIDER TREE -- LEAST headroom against a saturated spine; each node adds query positions + GDN-state bandwidth while branches keep accepting 0. Only helps behind a better drafter; net-negative until the drafter is fixed.

5. (excluded) Multi-spine -- CLOSED_NON_SHIP/lossy by directive; not a lossless lever.
synthesis.recommendation:
Headline (measured-only, decode_seconds basis): tree is 2.336x slower, decomposing EXACTLY into 1.432x more forwards x 1.632x more time-per-forward (~42% accept gap / ~58% per-forward tax) -- both factors are raw measured counters, never TPS/accept. Lead with this; the slower forward is the larger half.

Do-now: build/finish the WY one-pass GDN tree-scan (accept-only state commit) -- it is the only lever that moves the binding (per-forward) metric, removes the 9x GDN-state HBM amplification losslessly, and is already CPU-proven (4.19e-9, 0 flips). It targets the dominant ~58% share. The num_warps=8 spill fix is already committed; next close the ptxas spill-bytes==0 and bit-exact-at-N_PAD=16 LIVE gates.

Then run the CLEAN re-measurement that is the actual arbiter -- FR10_METRICS off, all FR12/FR13 capture-break hooks compiled out, WY kernel, B=4 CUDA-captured, vs E5 -- to replace the contaminated 1.632x with the true structural forward floor (est ~1.10-1.15x, UNMEASURED). That number decides everything.

Be honest about the ceiling: even with a clean ~1.0-1.10x forward, the tree only beats native if branches start adding net accepts (needs acc/event ~4.3-4.4 vs native 3.794), and branches have added 0 in every run -- so the lossless+fast win is conditional, thin (native is 76% of the depth-5 ceiling), and likely requires also fixing the caterpillar drafter (two known topology bugs) or deepening the drafter (lever 2, out of verify-kernel scope) to raise the ceiling. If the clean forward floor proves a hard >1.13x, no branch upside on a depth-5 spine breaks even, and the lossless-fast path is dead unless the drafter is deepened. Bring the clean-measurement pass/fail to the user before declaring win/loss.

overreaches: MINOR (already disclosed, not load-bearing): the absolute per-forward figure 0.4814 vs 0.2950 s/draft is decode_seconds/spec_drafts where decode_seconds is a per-request SUM across all 16 requests under B=4 concurrency (windows overlap), so it is NOT single-stream forward latency. The synthesis states this explicitly ('its absolute s/draft is not single-stream forward latency'); the RATIO 1.632x remains valid because both arms were measured identically. Not an overreach, just the limit of the basis.

MINOR (provenance precision): the kernel claims cite bare filename line numbers (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:582 etc.); the actual file is at src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py. All cited lines verify correctly there (num_warps=8 @582, h_cache @277, N_ACTUAL-masked stores @290-322, committer @85-203).

MINOR (estimate labeling — done correctly, noted for completeness): the +8.95%/+35.79% GDN-state amplification, the ~2.7% launch-tax ceiling, and the ~0.47% committer cost are CPU cost-model / first-principles arithmetic (gdn_cost_verify.py, bw_floor.py), NOT GPU-measured. The synthesis labels all of these as ESTIMATE and flags ptxas spill-bytes==0 + bit-exact-at-N_PAD=16 as un-certified live gates — so no estimate is presented as measured.

MINOR (cosmetic): cost model uses 48 layers while MEMORY's per-layer ladder references 64; the byte-percentage is a ratio (replay/native) and is invariant to layer count, so the +35.79% figure is unaffected.

It factors EXACTLY (algebraic identity, reproduced) into 1.432x more forwards (spec_drafts 620/433) x 1.632x more time-per-forward (decode_seconds/spec_drafts = 0.4814 vs 0.2950 s) -> log-share 42.3% / 57.7%. The per-forward number is measured/measured. The TPS/accept DERIVED ratios (warm_decode_tps, accepted_per_draft_event at probe.py:265-270) are explicitly quarantined and never used for the gap — the synthesis names and avoids the banned 1.412x/1.29x form. spec_drafts=forward-count is justified: spec_draft_tokens/spec_drafts = exactly 9.000 in both arms (=num_spec_tokens). No request_metrics.jsonl / steptrace in the run dir (confirmed), so per-kernel attribution of the 1.632x is correctly stated as UNKNOWN.
